qwen.scope: Single diagnostic traces; first and repeated load phases. Trace profiles, APKs, cache state and temperatures differ; no controlled latency-effect estimate.

llama.scope: Single diagnostic traces; first and repeated load phases. Trace profiles, APKs, cache state and temperatures differ; no controlled latency-effect estimate.

interpretation: The profile is a separate diagnostic runtime workload, not a matched untraced latency trial or the app journey trace.

Event ts/dur use microseconds relative to this ORT profile clock. Run indexes are timestamp-sorted; generation mapping is verified against two 8-token workload events and input shapes [1,32] then seven [1,1].

Session model_loading_uri is ORT model loading/deserialization, not app graph validation. session_initialization is a separate coarse ORT setup stage; it does not resolve graph optimization versus prepacking.
model_run, SequentialExecutor::Execute and Node events are nested. They must not be added together. Node sums are reported separately from interval unions and run wall time.

Operator durations are elapsed kernel-event durations, not CPU core-time. These recorded node intervals have the measured overlap shown above; scheduling/worker CPU utilization requires another source.
All profiled node events name CPUExecutionProvider; this workload provides no evidence of GPU/NPU execution.

The output-head weight is dequantized from uint8 [896,151936] to float [896,151936] on every run (544538624 output bytes). The profile proves repeated work, not a safe cache/quantization transformation.

Prefill computes lm_head logits for all 32 prompt positions, although the Java runtime reads only the final logits row. A last-token-only export is a candidate requiring separate output/reference parity and immutable-artifact provenance.
Time outside ORT node/run intervals includes runtime/harness work, scheduling and profiling effects; it is not automatically app verification or checksum overhead.
Only one warmup and one profiled generation are available. No throughput claim or setting recommendation is established by this diagnostic.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: Initial installed-load4128.48ms contains3403.22ms runtime; runtime graph559.72ms, tokenizer initialization926.65ms, session creation1851.04ms.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: Runtime reconstruction dominates. Repository+preparation overhead is about725ms in this diagnostic, not20seconds.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: Zero artifact.payloadChecksum slices, and app DI passes verifyContent=false; manifest+finalArtifact checks42.64ms initially,43.71ms on repeat.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: No evidence that full payload checksums are causing current ONNX load time. Reported SHA identities are stored publication evidence.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: Initial graph559.72ms has522.49ms caller CPU and30.00ms I/O wait; repeat468.08ms has446.14ms CPU and19.64ms I/O wait.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: Most time is active graph-validation work. Buffer small protobuf reads while preserving bounds/external-reference checks, then measure separately.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: Initial tokenizer926.65ms has918.36ms caller CPU; repeat564.26ms has564.23ms CPU. Initial tokenizer read52.30ms hasonly0.50ms I/O wait.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: Parsing/index construction dominates storage wait. Investigate allocation/object construction only after graph improvement; resident reuse avoids all repeated parsing.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: Initial session1851.04ms has1630.99ms caller CPU and203.76ms I/O wait; repeat1560.43ms has1551.46ms CPU and7.88ms I/O wait. kswapd CPU overlaps initial session by570.52ms.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: ORT session construction dominates even with little I/O on repeat. Reclaim/cache state contributes to initial-versus-repeat differences; exact session optimization/weight-prepacking split is not traced.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: First TTFT trace557.94ms contains477.81ms prefill,25.53ms tokenization,33.98ms argmax and8.53ms logits access. Warm TTFT302.95ms contains279.61ms prefill,3.30ms tokenization,1.05ms argmax and6.54ms logits access.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: First-generation initialization/JIT differs materially from warm inference. Do not discard first-generation cost when discussing user experience.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: Graph/tokenizer/session/prefill are DefaultDispatch synchronous slices; environment init45.29ms is instrumentation-thread work. Main UI thread runs3.34ms during4128.48ms load.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: No observed heavy ONNX work on main in this harness. ChatViewModel also launches production loading on Dispatchers.Default, but static-Activity traces do not test interactive chat rendering.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: Initial tokenizer overlaps42.21ms HeapTaskDaemon and117.54ms Jit-thread CPU; first generation overlaps89.39ms HeapTaskDaemon and695.04ms Jit CPU; warm generation72.99ms HeapTaskDaemon and12.69ms Jit CPU. No dalvik trace category or GC slices.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: Concurrent runtime housekeeping is measurable; GC stop-the-world duration and allocation ownership remain unmeasured. Add dalvik only to a separate diagnostic capture.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: RSS samples rise from~306to416MiB during tokenizer initialization,~557to1068MiB during initial session creation, then peak~1621MiB during first generation. Every ordinary trial grows sampled PSS by~78MiB from first tofourth short generation.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: Memory footprint/retention deserves a longer-run plateau test and allocation evidence. Four generations do not prove a leak. System VM samples show reclaim; no kernel OOM-kill counter increment occurs.

baselineTraceFindings.evidence: A third dispatcher worker uses511.58ms CPU duringfirst1446.77ms generation and357.30ms duringwarm955.27ms generation. PSS is polled every100ms plus its own collection time.
baselineTraceFindings.meaning: Strong source/topology evidence of benchmark sampling overhead, but source-named span was absent. Parent is adding explicit mode and sampler span; disabled sampling is a measurement change, not production optimization.

baselineMeasurementLimitations: Async repository spans have process tracks, so no caller thread is inferred from their track. Synchronous runtime spans identify actual worker threads.
CPU/state intersections are clipped per phase. Nested phases and all-thread CPU are not additive wall-time components.
Native-only capture has no dalvik category, heap allocation profiler or stacks; zero GC slices is missing coverage, not zero GC.
HeapTaskDaemon and Jit thread CPU are observed work; neither alone measures GC pause duration or assigns a specific allocation.
Process RSS is sampled every250ms and system VM counters every1s. Values are sampled bounds, not exact peaks or per-process page-fault attribution.
Initial session creation overlaps system reclaim and ~204ms caller I/O wait; kernel blocked-function names are absent, so exact fault/read cause is unresolved.
Static foreground validation Activity does not exercise production chat rendering. Initial reconciliation, inventory lookup, settings acquisition and repository construction precede whole_load_ms.
Generation resets/tokenizes the system prompt before TTFT. First-generation warmup is retained separately; subsequent generations keep the ORT session but recreate inference state.
Runtime first token and app first nonempty chunk are different scopes; output SHA proves recorded-text integrity, not semantic model quality.
Generation timing includes a100ms-period PSS sampler and its cancellation/join. The extra dispatcher CPU cannot be conclusively attributed without a sampler span.
Sparse runtime trace landmarks cover first two generated-token iterations and iteration8; missing decode spans are intentional, not idle gaps.
Perfetto process polling itself is visible as traced_probes CPU; ordinary passes are the latency evidence.
Identity stage compares reported prepared-artifact identities with pinned hashes. It is not an independent device rehash at that stage.

cycles.name: Background young concurrent mark compact GC

interpretation: Memory sample spans are process-scoped async slices with no tid. Their elapsed duration and overlap are directly measured; a specific sampler CPU cost is not attributable from this capture.
All-app CPU during sample intervals includes inference, GC/JIT and unrelated workers. It is not sampler CPU and must not be added to wall time.
GC cycle durations include concurrent collection. Only named MarkingPause/CompactionPause intervals are unioned as pause phases; nested (Paused) children and ThreadListFlip are not added again.

Explicit suspension scopes use Mutator threads suspended for ScopedPause and FlipThreadSuspension. Acquisition/resumption edges and per-thread root-flip delays mean these scopes are not an exhaustive per-thread suspension-time measurement.

AOSP ART source supports these marker interpretations (thread_list.cc SuspendAll/ResumeAll and FlipThreadRoots; collector garbage_collector.cc ScopedPause). Archived main-branch source is explanatory, not proven identical to the device ART build.
Native inference threads may run while Java mutators are paused. GC overlap alone is not equal to delay imposed on inference or proof of allocation ownership.
Llama has no dalvik category: null GC fields mean unmeasured, not zero GC.
Candidate Qwen uses full framework+dalvik tracing, whereas baseline used native-only tracing. These diagnostics locate work but are not controlled total-latency A/Bs.

limitations: One capture per model/build with uncontrolled cache, JIT, scheduler and memory conditions. Use matched ordinary multi-trial results for total latency conclusions.
Qwen candidate enables framework/dalvik tracing absent from baseline; Llama baseline/candidate both lack dalvik.

Graph-validation reduction is consistent with removing per-byte file syscalls. Tokenizer and ORT session implementation were not changed; differences in those stages are not attributed to the buffer optimization.
All observed graph spans retain validation and report zero instrumented payload checksums. Small Java hash/class-loading/JIT names are not file checksum work.

measurementLimitations: Fresh processes do not imply uncached storage; no page-cache flushing was performed.
Build and resident-reselection pairs have three processes per condition; the memory-polling comparison has only one process per condition.
Tracing is diagnostic and separate from ordinary timing; Qwen baseline and candidate capture profiles differ.
PSS sampling has process-scoped async spans. Wall time and overlap are measured; sampler-specific CPU time is unidentifiable.
Qwen full capture has ART pause evidence; Llama native-only capture has no GC visibility. Concurrent collection duration is not pause duration.
Short math answers, natural EOG and output hashes do not establish general output quality, long-generation speed or memory-retention behavior.
App TTFT ends at the first nonempty stream chunk; runtime benchmark token counts and prompt differ.
Installed load excludes Activity startup, startup reconciliation, inventory lookup and first drawn chat. Static harness foreground checks do not exercise interactive UI.
Prepared-artifact identities are compared with pinned publication metadata. The identity record is not an independent device rehash during timing.
Thermal and foreground checks are sampled/endpoints, not a controlled laboratory. See exact per-trial records.
